title: Regular base change for closed supported etale inverse image
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $r:P\to X$ be a morphism of Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible; Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume $r$ is regular, meaning flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] with geometrically regular fibres: the fibre over a point remains regular after every finite extension of its residue field [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and form $Z_P=P\times_XZ$ with projections $q:Z_P\to Z$ and $i_P:Z_P\hookrightarrow P$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use the small-etale bounded-below derived categories of $\Lambda$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], ordinary inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], which are exact by [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact], and the supported right derived inverse image $i^!$ of the functor $i^{-1}\ker(1\to j_*j^{-1})$, where $j$ is the complementary open immersion [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel]. For every $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ the canonical supported comparison is an isomorphism
$$q^*i^!M\xrightarrow{\sim}i_P^!r^*M.$$
The comparison is the adjunction mate of closed direct-image base change: after applying $i_{P*}$, its composite with the supported counit equals $r^*$ of the supported counit $i_*i^!M\to M$. These comparisons are natural in $M$, commute with Tate twists and shifts, and satisfy pasting for compositions of regular base changes and for compositions of closed immersions. They commute with restriction to open subschemes and localization at points, including the supported-composition identifications defining successive point costalks. No excellence, finite-type, compactifiability, or constructibility hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVII, Corollary 4.2.3 and its proof from Proposition 4.2.1; canonical supported comparison and its fibrewise use in Lemma 4.3.1.1. The pasting/localization clauses specify the canonical mate, not arbitrary comparison isomorphisms.
